articles.title: Visakhapatnam Steel Plant accident: eight dead in ladle blast, fire at SMS-1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eight workers were killed and six injured in a blast at the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL) plant in Visakhapatnam on Monday. The explosion, which occurred around 4:40 p.m., triggered a fire and spilled hundreds of tonnes of molten steel.  The injured sustained critical burn injuries.

articles.title: Home Minister, MP seek thorough probe into VSP tragedy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam MP M. Sribharat, Home Minister Vangalapudi Anita, and District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore reviewed rescue and relief efforts at the site of a fatal accident at the Steel Melting Shop-1 (SMS-1) of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.  They were briefed by steel plant officials on the circumstances leading to the mishap, rescue operations, safety protocols, and relief measures for affected workers and their families.

articles.title: First a blast, then molten steel at 1,500°C falls to floor: What we know about Vizag Steel Plant accident | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: An explosion at the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (RINL), also known as Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, resulted in the deaths of eight people on Monday. The incident occurred during casting operations at Caster-2 of Steel Melt Shop-1, where a crane carrying a ladle broke, causing molten steel to fall and engulf several workers.  Union Ministry of Steel, CITU trade union leader J Ayodhya Ram, and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) are involved in investigations into the cause of the explosion.

articles.title: Indian-origin restaurant owner in Texas says she doesn’t hire Indians: 'Our team doesn’t come from the same culture' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rashmi Bhat, owner of 7 Monk’s Cafe in Texas, sparked online discussion after stating that her Indian restaurant has “almost no Indian staff” and choosing to hire based on skills rather than ethnicity.  She explained that she aims to create a diverse team drawn from the local community, including high school students, college students, single mothers, and retirees seeking second chances. Bhat emphasized that her focus is on building a strong workforce regardless of cultural background, noting that many staff members initially lacked familiarity with Indian cuisine but learned the dishes over time.

articles.title: Inside Mithoon-Palak Muchhal's lavish home in Mumbai
articles.rephrased_article: Mithoon, Palak Muchhal, and filmmaker Farah Khan hosted a gathering at their Mumbai residence, showcasing the couple's understated luxury aesthetic. The home features warm tones, layered lighting, and sleek finishes in its living room, which boasts an elaborate false ceiling design and luxurious seating arrangement.  A walk-in closet designed for Palak Muchhal is another highlight of the space. The kitchen and balcony area also reflect the minimalist theme with beige and gold accents. Interior designer Mita Mehta emphasized that a home's aesthetic should be tailored to its residents, not just for social media presentation.

articles.title: Meta Deletes Face-Recognition System From Its Smart Glasses App After WIRED Report | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Meta removed an unreleased face-recognition system from its Meta AI app after a report by WIRED revealed its presence. The company, which initially denied the existence of the feature, now claims it was purely exploratory and has no plans to implement it.  Following the report, Meta removed nearly all traces of the system, including code libraries and folders related to face recognition. Privacy advocates like Kade Crockford, director of the technology for liberty program at the American Civil Liberties Union of Massachusetts, argue that this action doesn't undo the initial decision to ship the code and highlights the need for stronger consumer privacy laws.

articles.title: Japan Bear Attack: What Forced Nearly 100 Schools To Shut In Japan? A Bear
articles.rephrased_article: Authorities in Utsunomiya, Japan closed nearly 100 schools as a precaution after a bear was spotted roaming the city for three days. The animal, estimated to be one meter long, has been seen multiple times across the city, prompting residents to report sightings near homes, shopping arcades, parks, and even schools. Hunters, police, and local officials launched a major search operation, urging people to stay indoors or in vehicles.  The bear's presence highlights a growing trend of bear encounters in urban areas due to climate change and habitat changes.

articles.title: Apple’s New Siri AI Is Ready to Get Personal | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple announced a major overhaul of its Siri voice assistant, partnering with Google Gemini to enhance its AI model. The revamp includes a stand-alone Siri app, chatbot interactions, and access to personal data for more personalized responses. This move comes after years of competition from other AI assistants like Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude, and OpenAI's ChatGPT, which have surpassed Apple's Siri in capabilities.  Apple aims to deliver a more powerful and user-friendly experience with this update, but concerns remain about privacy as the company utilizes personal data for improved functionality.

articles.title: Senior Lawyer Sriram Panchu Alleges Accessibility Lapses, Dress Code Row At Madras Club
articles.rephrased_article: Sriram Panchu, a senior lawyer and mediator, filed a complaint against the Madras Club in Chennai after allegedly falling due to an uneven pathway.  Panchu, who uses a cane or wheelchair for mobility, claims he repeatedly raised concerns about the unsafe route with club management but the issue remained unresolved. He also expressed dissatisfaction over dress code enforcement, alleging that his guest was reprimanded for attire deemed inappropriate. The Madras Club disputes these accusations and maintains its commitment to disability access and adherence to dress code regulations.

articles.title: Apple’s iPhone Camera App Is Getting an AI Upgrade in iOS 27 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple unveiled new features for its iOS 27 operating system, including a redesigned camera app with Siri AI integration. The feature allows users to access visual assistance like Google Lens directly within the camera app, making it easier to use. Apple is also introducing AI-powered editing tools to the Photos app, such as Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing, which enhance image quality and perspective. These features are expected to debut on select iPhones later this year.

articles.title: Guns N’ Roses lock in mega 2026 India tour with stops in Bengaluru and Guwahati | Music News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Guns N' Roses will perform in Guwahati, India on November 17, 2026, as part of their ongoing world tour. The concert is being organized by the Assam government and follows a successful performance by Post Malone last year.  The band’s visit marks their third time performing in India, with previous tours including stops in Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru.

articles.title: Indian men in Canada praised for saving distressed woman from harasser at cricket ground in viral video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A video of Indian men in British Columbia, Canada, intervening to protect a woman from harassment at a cricket ground has garnered attention online. The incident highlights positive aspects of the Indian community and contrasts with recent viral videos that portrayed Indians negatively.  The men spoke to the alleged stalker, asking him to stay away and ultimately leading him to leave the scene peacefully.

articles.title: FIFA asks small Vancouver pet shop to take down plush bears wearing World Cup jerseys
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA is concerned about plush bears displayed in a Vancouver pet shop, claiming they infringe on its trademark. Dawn Moulton, owner of Cascadia Natural Pet Supply, dressed 20 plush bears in football jerseys and promoted them online. She was asked to remove the items or face fines over violation of FIFA trademark rules.  Moulton believes this action is illogical and feels like a corporate attempt to stifle small businesses and profit from events.

articles.title: Quote of the day by American astronomer Marc Aaronson: “If we are going to die anyway...why be cautious? Why not risk all now, at this moment, in this adventure?” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marc Aaronson's quote, "If we are going to die anyway...why be cautious? Why not risk all now, at this moment, in this adventure?", challenges the tendency for people to delay action due to fear of failure.  While caution can provide safety, it can also prevent meaningful experiences and opportunities from being pursued. Aaronson argues that uncertainty is inherent in life and encourages readers to consider whether avoiding action is as safe as it appears. He emphasizes that history reveals that those who take risks are often the ones who achieve success, while those who hesitate may regret missed opportunities.

articles.title: 8 Workers Killed At Vizag Steel Plant As Molten Iron Spills
articles.rephrased_article: Eight workers at the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd (Vizag Steel Plant) were killed and six others injured when molten iron spilled on them.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences and offered an ex-gratia of Rs 2 lakh to the families of the deceased and Rs 50,000 to the injured. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu also expressed his grief and directed relief measures. The incident occurred at 4:15 pm on Monday when molten iron was being moved in a bucket by a crane.

articles.title: Watch Duty Is Adding Flood Alerts to Its Wildfire App | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Watch Duty, a wildfire alert app, has expanded its service to include flood alerts. The nonprofit, which started in 2021 and uses volunteers and paid employees to monitor emergency responder radio channels, will now provide users with information about flood zones and water levels through push notifications. John Mills, CEO of Watch Duty, believes the app can help people make informed decisions by consolidating information from various agencies like FEMA, the National Weather Service, and NOAA into a single platform.  Watch Duty plans to expand its coverage to include all natural disasters in the future.

Aaronson's words resonate with many because they touch on a fear of looking back and realizing that caution prevented something meaningful.

articles.title: New device may make computers 1,000 times faster without overheating while reducing data center power consumption | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new research paper published in Science describes a light-driven switching device that could revolutionize computing by enabling ultrafast information processing. The device, based on an antiferromagnetic material, switches states in 40 picoseconds, significantly faster than conventional semiconductor logic which operates in the sub-nanosecond range. This technology has the potential to reduce energy consumption in data centers by eliminating the need for continuous electrical current and its associated heat generation. However, scaling up this technology to industrial levels faces challenges related to material availability and manufacturing complexity.  The research suggests that a hybrid system combining optical triggering with magnetic non-volatile storage could offer significant performance improvements while reducing idle power consumption.

articles.title: Priyanka Chopra once 'kicked' designer shoes on set, says Quantico stylist Cary Tauben
articles.rephrased_article: Priyanka Chopra, styled by Cary Tauben, impressed audiences with her performance in the action thriller "Quantico".  Tauben shared anecdotes about Chopra's demanding nature during fittings, while Dr Rimpa Sarkar, a clinical psychologist, explained how pep talks and affirmations can help individuals manage stress and boost confidence. These techniques, according to Sarkar, can improve concentration, reduce anxiety, and increase motivation, ultimately leading to better performance outcomes.

articles.title: Esha Deol on mother Hema Malini accepting late father Dharmendra's Padma Vibhushan: 'Deeply emotional'
articles.rephrased_article: Esha Deol, daughter of late Bollywood legend Dharmendra, shared her grief over his passing, stating that she misses him every day.  She also expressed her pride in her mother, Hema Malini, accepting the Padma Vibhushan on Dharmendra's behalf, acknowledging the family's wish for him to have received the award earlier in life. Deol emphasized that awards were never important to her father and he valued people's love above all else.  She considers herself fortunate to be the daughter of such iconic figures and hopes to instill their values in her own children.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Nikola Tesla: “If your hate could be turned into electricity, it would light up the whole world.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nikola Tesla's quote, "If your hate could be turned into electricity, it would light up the whole world," highlights the immense energy consumed by negative emotions like hatred. The quote, which draws a comparison between the power of hatred and the vastness of electricity, emphasizes how much time and mental energy people often devote to resentment, leading to lasting consequences in personal relationships and societal conflicts.  The enduring popularity of this quote stems from its relatable observation about human behavior and its ability to prompt reflection on how we direct our emotional energy.

articles.title: Apple WWDC 2026 Live Blog: All the Updates, as They Happen | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple's annual Worldwide Developer Conference (WWDC) 2026 is set to begin at 10 am Pacific, 1 pm Eastern, and 6 pm British Summer Time. articles.title: Momfluencers Are Pitching AI as a Better ‘Coparent’ Than Men | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Lilian Schmidt, a brand consultant from Zurich, turned to ChatGPT after struggling with her daughter's sleep and found success. She became an advocate for using AI as a parenting tool, leading to the creation of her own AI assistant called Coparent.  Other women like Sarah Dooley are also embracing AI to delegate household tasks, but concerns about environmental impact and potential job displacement remain. Some critics argue that framing AI as a feminist tool is misplaced, while others believe it can help alleviate the mental load on mothers. Despite these concerns, many moms see AI as a way to reclaim their time and reduce stress.

articles.title: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5x Review: The Best Laptop Under $1,000 | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: WIRED and Lenovo have released the IdeaPad Slim 5x laptop. The laptop features a 15.3-inch display, 16GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. It offers good performance for everyday tasks and comes with a fast 120Hz refresh rate.  The laptop also has excellent battery life, lasting over 22 hours on a single charge. The IdeaPad Slim 5x is available for purchase at $850.

articles.title: 3 Air India A320 Aircraft Damaged At Delhi Airport After Strong Winds
articles.rephrased_article: Three Air India A320 aircraft parked at Delhi airport's Terminal 2 were damaged by strong winds during adverse weather conditions on Sunday afternoon. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) launched an investigation into the incident, which involved ground support equipment striking two planes and a third suffering damage from debris. All three aircraft have been grounded for inspection and repairs.

articles.title: Meta testing Hatch AI assistant as AI race with OpenAI, Anthropic heats up: Report | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Meta is reportedly developing an AI agent called Hatch to compete with rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic. The company is considering a tiered pricing structure for Hatch, positioning it as a premium offering similar to ChatGPT Pro and Claude Max.  Hatch could be integrated into Meta-owned services, potentially reaching billions of users. Meta aims to leverage AI-powered agents like Hatch to generate sustainable revenue streams from its investments in the field.

articles.title: Second theft: How scammers use a lost iPhone to steal your identity | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: I4C has issued an advisory warning of a new phishing scam targeting Apple users. Perpetrators impersonate Apple Support officials, exploiting victims' urgency to locate or secure their missing devices through fraudulent SMS messages containing phishing links. These messages appear legitimate and redirect users to counterfeit Apple login pages designed to steal Apple ID credentials and one-time passwords (OTP). Once the stolen device is compromised, attackers gain unauthorized access to victims’ accounts and remove the linked Apple IDs from the devices.  The government advisory recommends avoiding clicking links received through SMS or unsolicited messages, verifying website addresses before entering credentials, and using official Apple channels for verification.

articles.title: Delhi-NCR Weather Today, 8 June Live: Weather Office Predicts More Rain In Delhi-NCR
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast very light to light rainfall, accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds of up to 60 kmph for Delhi-NCR on June 11 and 12.  These conditions are expected to bring down the maximum temperature to around 35-37 degrees Celsius on June 12. The southwest monsoon made its onset over Kerala on June 4, three days later than its normal date, but weather experts expect it to advance steadily and cover most parts of the country by the third week of June.  The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has issued a warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching speeds of 40 to 50 kmph in parts of Tamil Nadu, particularly along the Western Ghats, over the next few days. The IMD also reported that rainfall continued at isolated places in Rajasthan with the maximum rain of 93.

articles.title: Ahmedabad plane crash: A year on, victim’s father rebuilds life; says son kept his promise even after death - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Girdharbhai Kalawadia, a 62-year-old man, continues to grieve the loss of his filmmaker son, Mahesh Jirawala, who died in the June 2022 Air India crash.  Despite the immense pain, Kalawadia is grateful for the compensation received from Air India, the Tata Group, and the Gujarat government which enabled him to purchase a home for his family. The family used the funds to pay off debts, purchase furniture, and provide for their granddaughter. Kartik, Kalawadia's younger son, now runs a hair-cutting salon to support the family financially.

articles.title: Ahmedabad Air India plane crash: Grief shapes lives of people on the ground
articles.rephrased_article: A year after the Air India crash at BJ Medical College in Ahmedabad, the impact of the tragedy continues to be felt.  The wreckage remains, and students and residents grapple with grief and a sense of permanent loss. The families of those killed are still searching for answers, while others struggle with physical injuries or emotional trauma. Officials have approved plans to demolish the damaged complex and rebuild, but the scars remain. Meenakshi Parikh, the dean of BJ Medical College, continues to navigate the college's return to normalcy amidst overwhelming grief.

articles.title: How to watch Apple WWDC 2026 keynote live: Check date, timings, what to expect | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Apple Inc.'s annual developer conference, WWDC 2026, will take place from June 8-12 at Apple's headquarters in Cupertino, California. The event will feature the opening keynote presentation on Monday, June 8th, where Tim Cook, current CEO of Apple, is expected to make his final appearance as CEO and John Ternus, senior vice president of hardware engineering, will take over in September.  The keynote will also include the debut of iOS 27, a new Siri, and potentially new Mac devices. The conference is significant for Apple's software division, especially its AI ambitions following the launch of Apple Intelligence at WWDC 2024.

articles.title: Success Story | From Tapa Mandi to Chandigarh tech trailblazer, the growth of Beesolver | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sumit Singh, founder and CEO of Beesolver Technology Pvt Ltd, built his successful technology firm on a foundation of trust, relationships, and values. articles.title: Work begins to provide online tickets for darshan in T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR & CE) Department is implementing an online ticket system for darshan in large temples across the state to streamline the process. articles.title: Latest trouble for Khan Sir’s institute: Fire safety ‘shortcomings’ | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Bihar Fire Services conducted a fire safety audit at Khan Global Studies in Patna, identifying multiple deficiencies and issuing a notice requiring the institution to rectify them within a week. The inspection follows recent fatal fire incidents in Delhi and Muzaffarpur, prompting the state government to intensify fire safety checks across Bihar. Assistant District Fire Officer Ajay Kumar Sharma stated that the institute lacked a fire alarm system, fire pump, and inadequate water tank capacity.  Bihar Fire Services DIG Manoj Kumar Nut emphasized the department's stricter approach following recent tragedies, warning of potential sealing action if compliance is not ensured.

articles.title: Sameera reddy's Modern Family Goes Beyond the "Sasu-Bahu" Script
articles.rephrased_article: Sameera Reddy shares a warm and supportive relationship with her mother-in-law, a dynamic that highlights the importance of emotional safety in family relationships. He suggests that warmth and openness create an environment where individuals can express themselves authentically, fostering genuine connections beyond traditional roles.

articles.title: Child falls into septic tank at construction site in Kasaragod, dies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A six-year-old boy, Mohammed Ayan Shasim, tragically died after falling into a septic tank at a construction site in Kasaragod, India. The lack of safety measures around the septic tank has sparked criticism and raised concerns about negligence at the site.

The Jai Mahal Palace, now owned by the Taj Hotels Group, offers accommodations, fine dining options, and a spa. The palace is a popular tourist destination and serves as a symbol of Jaipur's rich history and culture.

articles.title: 2 Pet Dogs Die, 7 Residents Rescued From Fire In Delhi's New Friends Colony
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out in a house in New Friends Colony, Delhi, trapping seven residents on the upper floors due to thick smoke and blocked main staircase. Delhi Fire Service (DFS) personnel responded with specialized equipment and water bowsers, rescuing all seven residents, including four children, safely. Police are investigating the cause of the fire.

articles.title: MEIL-led Zojila tunnel set for final breakthrough on June 9 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Megha Engineering & Infrastructure Ltd. (MEIL) and the National Highways & Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd. (NHIDCL) are set to celebrate a key milestone with the final breakthrough of the Zojila Tunnel scheduled for June 9th. Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari is expected to attend the ceremony.

articles.title: How farming made Salim Kumar a ‘billionaire’ and earned even Mammootty’s praise | Malayalam News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Salim Kumar, a legendary actor from Kerala, passed away on June 6th.  Known for his comedic roles and outspoken political views, Kumar was deeply passionate about agriculture and actively practiced farming for many years. He believed that farming provided immense satisfaction and even claimed it could make someone a billionaire, earning praise from fellow actor Mammootty.  Kumar owned agricultural land in Kerala where he cultivated Pokkali rice, vegetables, and fish, often speaking out on issues facing farmers.

articles.title: Why RGV believes Obsession is a masterclass for filmmakers: ‘No big stars, no heavy VFX’ | Hollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Ram Gopal Varma, a renowned Indian filmmaker, has expressed his admiration for the American supernatural psychological horror film "Obsession," praising its success despite minimal production costs.  He believes that the movie's modest budget and lack of reliance on big stars or elaborate visual effects have contributed to its global box office success exceeding $178 million. Varma highlighted the film's unique editing style, sound design, and psychological depth as key factors in its appeal. He also noted that "Obsession" has challenged traditional filmmaking conventions by emphasizing emotional connection over spectacle.

articles.title: Four workers die after inhaling toxic fumes at septic tank in Surat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four workers died at a jewellery manufacturing unit in Surat, Gujarat on Sunday after allegedly inhaling toxic fumes from a septic tank. Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zone-1, Alok Kumar stated that asphyxiation is likely the cause of death and a postmortem report will confirm the exact cause. The incident occurred at the septic tank used for waste collection in the Ashwini Kumar area.

articles.title: Wildlife sanctuaries to visit in and around Delhi this summer vacation | Pets-animals News - The Indian Express

These sanctuaries cater to various interests, from birdwatching to photography and trekking, offering unique opportunities to reconnect with nature.

articles.title: Bombay High Court to consider interim safeguards for advocates as protection law put on hold | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay High Court is considering interim safeguards for advocates in Maharashtra, where a bill protecting them from violence and intimidation has been introduced but not yet enacted. The court heard arguments from the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa, who argued that existing provisions are inadequate, and representatives of the central government, who stated the legislation is pending with the Law Commission. Senior advocate Rajiv Chavan and advocate Satyavrat Joshi, appointed as amici curiae, suggested guidelines for protecting advocates until a law is enacted, including police protection and grievance redressal mechanisms. The court will deliberate on the issue at its next hearing on June 18th.

The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) responded to the blaze, which started on the first floor due to a malfunctioning air-conditioner unit. Two pet dogs trapped inside the building died as a result of smoke inhalation. The fire was extinguished within half an hour and all residents escaped unharmed.

articles.title: Thread by thread, Pochampally's weavers bring a living tradition to Hyderabad - The Hindu

The handloom tradition is captivating visitors who witness the meticulous craftsmanship behind the vibrant pink fabric.

articles.title: Veerappan’s claim: Actor Sukanya wins defamation case after 30 years - The Hindu

Sukanya for airing a 1996 interview with forest brigand Veerappan, which included scandalous allegations against her without editing them out. articles.title: Motorists flag dangerous aquaplaning hotspots on NH 66 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Motorists on the newly widened National Highway-66 between Kozhikode and Malappuram districts are raising concerns about aquaplaning hotspots, particularly along the overtaking lane where speeds frequently exceed 80 kmph. National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) officials acknowledge the issue and plan to inspect suspected hotspots for remedial measures. Kerala State Road Transport Corporation drivers suggest warning blinkers or signboards as immediate solutions while Motor Vehicles department (MVD) officers have already brought the matter to higher authorities' attention.

articles.title: Kerala Agricultural University releases new green chilli variety - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala Agricultural University (KAU) has released KAU Thejaswini, a new green chilli variety developed for the state's farming conditions. articles.title: Madhavan on why he never cheated on wife Sarita: ‘I’m a darpok Madrasi middle-class man’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Madhavan, who recently celebrated his 27th wedding anniversary with wife Sarita, attributes his loyalty to family and a "darpok (coward) Madrasi middle-class man" mentality. articles.title: Traffic diversions for Fish Prasadam event in Hyderabad’s Nampally on June 8-9 - The Hindu

The police will implement the diversions as needed to ensure safe traffic flow.

articles.title: Dubai-based Indian man, wife killed in Kerala road crash; daughter survives after last-minute car switch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A tragic road accident in Kerala claimed the lives of a Dubai-based Indian man, his wife, and his aunt. Shafid Ebrahim (40), an interior designer working in Dubai, was driving with his family when their car collided with a lorry parked on the roadside.  The family had stopped for tea before the accident, and the daughter, Sanfa Fatima, switched to another vehicle during the break. articles.title: Two killed as truck, car collide in Pathanamthitta - The Hindu

Fire and Rescue Services personnel extricated the injured occupants from the wreckage.

articles.title: Excessive AI Use Is Like Porn Addiction: Palantir CEO Alex Karp Slams Tokenmaxxing
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir, criticized businesses for focusing too much on AI usage without demonstrating its value. articles.title: Tunnel To Connect Delhi And Noida Airports? Inside Centre's Big Plan
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) have initiated feasibility studies for a Noida-Delhi tunnel to reduce traffic congestion. articles.title: Priya Bapat recalls co-star kissing her repeatedly on set: ‘Didn’t know how to deal with it’ | Web-series News - The Indian Express

articles.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu reveals Sai Pallavi was first choice for Maa Inti Bangaaram | Telugu News - The Indian Express

articles.rephrased_article: Lauf, an Icelandic brand known for its innovative front suspension, has launched the eElja electric mountain bike. articles.title: You May Not Need a Giant Chef’s Knife When a Midsize Knife Does the Trick | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Messermeister, Zwilling, and Cangshan knives are gaining popularity for their midsize designs. The knives' performance varied depending on the task, with some excelling at slicing and others better suited for chopping or rocking cuts. The price range for these midsize knives is from $120 (Zwilling) to $220 (Takayuki kiritsuke), making them a viable option for home cooks and professionals alike.

articles.title: Sigma BF Review (2026): Eccentric but Strangely Lovable | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Sigma has released the BF camera, a unique model that lacks traditional features like a mechanical shutter and viewfinder. articles.title: Senior Royals Gather As King Charles' Nephew Marries Nurse Harriet Sperling
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Queen Camilla attended the wedding of Peter Phillips, son of Princess Anne, to Harriet Sperling, an NHS nurse, in Kemble village. articles.title: Massive Fire Burns Down 8 Shops In Jammu And Kashmir's Poonch District
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at Bufliaz market in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch district caused extensive damage to eight shops, but no casualties were reported.  The fire, which broke out around 5 am, was brought under control within 30 minutes with the help of local residents, the army, and CRPF personnel. Preliminary investigation suggests a short circuit as the cause, while locals demand a permanent fire station due to repeated risks. The fire has left several families without their primary source of livelihood.

articles.title: How to Watch Apple’s WWDC 2026 Keynote—and What to Expect | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Apple CEO Tim Cook will host the company's annual Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) on June 8th, where he is expected to announce new software features for Siri, iOS, and Apple's artificial intelligence efforts. The keynote address will likely focus on enhancing performance across its operating systems, including iOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and more. Apple is also rumored to introduce AI-powered features like digital pass creation and receipt splitting for Siri, as well as a potential foldable device announcement later this year.

articles.title: 1965-Built Monastery Thangu Sertok Gumpa Destroyed In Sikkim Fire, Religious Artefacts Damaged
articles.rephrased_article: A fire destroyed the Thangu Sertok Gumpa monastery and two nearby houses in North Sikkim on June 5th. The blaze, reportedly caused by an electrical short circuit, spread rapidly through the structure, leaving no chance to salvage any religious or cultural artifacts.  The monastery, built in 1965, held immense religious and cultural significance for the local community. Despite efforts to contain the flames, the fire reduced the monastery to ashes. No casualties were reported but significant property damage occurred.

articles.title: LG’s billionaire chairman spotted grilling meat for NVIDIA's CEO
articles.rephrased_article: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, met with senior business leaders from South Korea's corporate sector at a Korean barbecue restaurant in Seoul. articles.title: Former Meta Engineer Quits Tech Job to Open Noodles Stall in Singapore
articles.rephrased_article: A former Meta engineer, Alvin Tan, is making a name for himself as a Hokkien Mee hawker after leaving his tech career. articles.title: Dimple Hayathi, Ashika defend Janhvi Kapoor amid Peddi backlash: ‘Blame the system’ | Telugu News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Dimple Hayathi, Ashika Ranganath, and Anasuya Bharadwaj have weighed in on the controversy surrounding Janhvi Kapoor's portrayal in the Telugu film "Peddi."  They argue that actresses should not be blamed for the problematic storylines, but rather the system and makers who perpetuate such narratives. Dimple Hayathi emphasized the structural limitations faced by actresses and called for a shift in focus from blaming individuals to addressing systemic issues. Anasuya Bharadwaj, while acknowledging the influence of cinema on society, advocated for greater awareness and responsibility between creators and audiences.  The controversy stems from the film's portrayal of a romance track that some viewers perceive as normalizing harassment.

articles.title: Do AI bots now outnumber humans online? Here’s what Cloudflare’s Matthew Prince says | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Cloudflare CEO and co-founder Matthew Prince announced that AI agent traffic has surpassed human traffic online for the first time in internet history.  Prince noted that this milestone occurred sooner than anticipated, with bot traffic now comprising 57.5% of internet traffic compared to 42.5% for human web traffic. The surge in AI agent activity is attributed to these agents performing tasks such as browsing websites, comparing prices, and acting as personal assistants.  However, human users still dominate other metrics like time spent on apps and streaming services.

articles.title: In A First, Vijay Promotes 300 Engineers Of Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Ltd issued promotion orders to 300 assistant executive engineers (electrical) who joined the service between 2000 and 2002. The move, a first for the state-owned corporation, was granted in a transparent manner to address staffing needs and resolve long-pending promotion issues. C Joseph Vijay, the new Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, is credited with overseeing this significant event.

articles.title: Salim Kumar: the ultimate meme king - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Salim Kumar, a Malayalam actor, became a social media sensation with his characters and witty dialogues finding enduring popularity in memes.  He credits the meme culture for helping him make a successful comeback to the film industry after three years away due to poor health. Kumar remarked that even characters from flop films brought back memories about those long-forgotten films. He is known for his off-screen persona, often joking about being "killed" in fake news reports.

articles.title: Police Officer turned Love Island US contestant faces backlash
articles.rephrased_article: A Pennsylvania police officer, Sean Reifel, has faced backlash for leaving his job to participate in the reality TV show *Love Island USA*.  The mayor of Bethlehem expressed disappointment over Reifel's departure and noted the vacant position cannot be filled until next year. The controversy has sparked debate among residents, with some supporting Reifel's decision while others criticize it as a misuse of taxpayer funds for training. Reifel's family defended his choice, arguing that his appearance on the show could benefit the community and improve perceptions of law enforcement.

articles.title: Ilaiyaraaja: The Indian maestro still reshaping music 50 years on
articles.rephrased_article: Ilaiyaraaja, a renowned Indian composer, has left an indelible mark on music with his eclectic style and prolific output.  He revolutionized Tamil film music in the 1970s, blending traditional folk and classical influences with Western symphonic elements. His compositions have become iconic, earning him widespread acclaim and numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan. Ilaiyaraaja's enduring legacy continues to inspire a new generation of musicians and audiences alike.

articles.title: Salim Kumar: a mimicry artiste par excellence before taking over the film arena - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Salim Kumar, a renowned mimicry artist, achieved fame and success in the film industry after winning numerous university-level contests. articles.title: Padma Vibhushan N Rajam reflects on Banaras, music and a lifetime with the violin | Eye News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Padma Vibhushan N Rajam, a renowned violinist, has been awarded the Padma Vibhushan for her lifelong reimagination of the violin.  She adapted the technique of a European instrument to Hindustani vocal music, creating a unique style that blended Carnatic and Hindustani traditions. Rajam's musical journey began under the tutelage of her father and later with renowned musician Pt Omkarnath Thakur. She became known for her ability to seamlessly integrate classical ragas into her violin playing.  She has also trained several generations of musicians, including her daughter and granddaughters, who have released an album blending Hindustani music with contemporary orchestrations. Rajam continues to perform and teach, dedicated to sharing her passion for music.

articles.title: Ganga-Jamuni Tehzeeb: Why Lucknow still offers finest lessons in coexistence | Eye News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: SP Singh, founder of Lucknow Public School and Lucknow Public College of Professional Studies, is a prominent educational visionary in modern Uttar Pradesh who embodies the spirit of Ganga-Jamuni tehzeeb. UNESCO recognized Lucknow as a Creative City of Gastronomy for its unique approach to food and culture, emphasizing the importance of exchange and understanding across differences.

articles.title: This app lets users control robotic arms from anywhere using a phone | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Georgia Institute of Technology researchers have developed a system called COBALT that allows users to control robotic arms using their smartphones.  The platform, which transforms smartphones into motion controllers, enables basic actions such as picking up and moving objects without requiring prior robotics knowledge. COBALT aims to make robotics accessible to individuals worldwide by leveraging a network of smartphone users to gather data for AI training.  This technology has the potential to expand access to robotics education and create new commercial applications for remote robot assistance in various settings.

articles.title: ‘Jo ukhadna hai ukhad lo’: Shilpa Shinde reacts to backlash over false allegation row | Television News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Shilpa Shinde, an actor, has faced backlash for admitting that sexual harassment allegations she made against a Bhabiji Ghar Par Hain producer were false. articles.title: Five killed, two injured as car rams truck in Gujarat’s Morbi - The Hindu

articles.title: IndiGo flight from Singapore delayed after bird hit in Vijayawada - The Hindu

articles.title: Malayalam actor Salim Kumar dies at 56 | Malayalam News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Salim Kumar, a National Award-winning Malayalam actor, died at 56 from cardiac arrest in Kochi on Saturday. articles.title: Officials to inspect annadhanam scheme at Tiruchendur temple - The Hindu

articles.title: Sushmita Sen Says Being Thin Is Not Being Fit
articles.rephrased_article: Sushmita Sen, former Miss Universe, advocates for a holistic approach to fitness that goes beyond simply being thin. Dr. Ankit Poddar, a consultant surgeon at Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, explains that while someone may appear slim, they could still be "skinny fat" or have metabolically obese normal weight (MONW) due to high body fat and low muscle mass. articles.title: Imtiaz Ali Reflects on Love and Emotional Honesty in the Gen Z Era
articles.rephrased_article: Imtiaz Ali, a renowned filmmaker, discussed the evolving understanding of love among Gen Z. articles.title: Versatile actor Salim Kumar passes away aged 57 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Salim Kumar, a National Award-winning actor, writer, director, and mimicry artiste, passed away on June 6th at the age of 57 from cardiac arrest while receiving treatment. articles.rephrased_article: Vikram Bhatt, a filmmaker, spent 70 days in Udaipur jail following his arrest for a dispute over a proposed biopic about the late wife of Ajay Murdia, founder of Indira IVF.  During his incarceration, he experienced health issues and forged friendships with fellow inmates who provided him support. After his release, several Bollywood stars reached out to him, including Mithun Chakraborty and Sanjay Dutt, while Ajay Devgn called because of their long-standing friendship.  The filmmaker maintains that the charges against him are baseless and he is confident the truth will prevail in court. He is currently preparing for the release of his horror thriller "Haunted 3D: Echoes of the Past" on June 12th.

articles.title: Hemkund Sahib Yatra 2026: How to reach, trek route, and what pilgrims should know | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of devotees are participating in the annual Hemkund Sahib Yatra, a pilgrimage to the revered Sikh shrine in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district. The first batch of pilgrims was flagged off from Rishikesh on May 20th, with over 1.11 lakh registrations already received.  The journey begins at Govindghat and involves a challenging trek to Hemkund Sahib, which is situated at an altitude of 4,632 meters. Pilgrims are advised to carry appropriate clothing and check weather conditions before embarking on the pilgrimage.

articles.title: Auroville residents want more meaningful role in its present and future - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Auroville residents are calling for greater transparency in decision-making processes affecting the international township, citing concerns about land use, ecology, and community relations.  Several actors, including Piyush Manush, Vetrimaaran, and Andrea Jeremiah, visited an exhibition titled “Auroville: An Experiment Under Threat,” where residents expressed their desire for greater resident participation in decisions that impact the community they have built over the past 60 years.  Sindhuja Jagadeesh, a member of the Auroville Town Development Council, defended the development trajectory, stating that land exchanges were conducted legally and allegations of environmental destruction are unfounded. Anuradha Majumdar, a member of the Residents’ Assembly, emphasized the need for sturdy roads as part of the Master Plan and highlighted the minimal number of trees felled during construction.

articles.title: 14-year-old schoolboy dies in accident in Kollam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 14-year-old boy, Salman Faris, tragically died after being struck by a truck near Palkulangara in Kollam, Kerala. The accident occurred when the boy's mother was riding a scooter and attempted to overtake a truck, causing a collision with another two-wheeler.  The impact threw both riders off the scooter, and Salman was fatally run over by the truck. National highway development work is ongoing in the area, contributing to traffic congestion and narrow roads.

articles.title: American student Weston Higginbotham found dead in Japan after ChatGPT argument with mother
articles.rephrased_article: Weston Higginbotham, a junior at Auburn University studying biosystems engineering, was found deceased by a volunteer search-and-rescue group in a mountainous area outside of Kyoto.  The 20-year-old's disappearance followed an argument with his mother over the family's reliance on artificial intelligence during their trip to Japan. Weston opposed the use of large language models due to their environmental impact and was known for his pacifist beliefs. The search involved multiple agencies, including the Japanese police, US State Department, FBI, and Alabama officials.  The Higginbotham family expressed gratitude for the support they received during this difficult time.

articles.title: The Hindu Huddle concludes with evocative musical performance by former diplomat Nirupama Rao - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nirupama Rao, former Foreign Secretary, concluded the Hindu Huddle 2026 with a musical performance that spanned genres and cultures.  The performance, which included songs by Stephen Foster, Charlie Chaplin, and Bob Dylan, was accompanied by Sri Lankan pianist Soundarie David Rodrigo.  Rao spoke about how music has been an enduring constant in her life, serving as both a reflection of her travels and experiences and a tool for diplomacy. The closing session marked the end of the two-day event.

articles.title: The Hindu Huddle | Manoj Bajpayee wants an image makeover - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manoj Bajpayee, a seasoned actor, engaged in a lively discussion at The Hindu Huddle on June 6th.  He shared anecdotes about his early career struggles and expressed both support for technological advancements like AI while emphasizing the unique authenticity of human performance. Bajpayee also discussed the need for better recognition and financial support for independent films in India, highlighting the success of unconventional cinema abroad. He will next be seen in "Governor," a film based on the 1990 Indian economic crisis, where he plays former Reserve Bank of India Governor S. Venkitaramanan.

articles.title: Memories, Medium, or Message? Art as mirror to a world in transition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shilo Shiv Suleman, Seema Kohli, and Abhishek Poddar discussed the role of art in reflecting societal changes during a session at The Hindu Huddle.  They emphasized that art, particularly through mediums like murals, can be a powerful force for change, especially during times of fear and trauma. Narayan Lakshman, Opinion Editor, The Hindu, moderated the discussion, highlighting how art helps societies tell their stories and create meaning in moments of profound change.  The panellists agreed that art transcends traditional activism by offering a unique perspective on societal issues.

articles.title: American student Weston Higginbotham found dead in Japan after ChatGPT argument with mother
articles.rephrased_article: Weston Higginbotham, a junior at Auburn University, was found deceased by a volunteer search-and-rescue group in a mountainous area outside of Kyoto.  The 20-year-old's disappearance followed an argument with his mother, Nancy Higginbotham, over the family's reliance on artificial intelligence during their trip to Japan. The US State Department, FBI, and Alabama officials offered support throughout the investigation. The family launched their own private search efforts after the police search ended, and a volunteer search-and-rescue group later found Weston's body.

articles.title: Memories, Medium, or Message? Art as mirror to a world in transition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shilo Shiv Suleman, award-winning artist, and Seema Kohli discussed the role of art in a world undergoing profound change at The Hindu Huddle. Narayan Lakshman, Opinion Editor, The Hindu, moderated the session which also included Abhishek Poddar, an art collector.  The panellists explored how art can shape collective opinion and create a middle ground in a deeply polarized world.

articles.title: 13.5 Million Km, 80,000 Words: Shubhanshu Shukla Brings Space Down To Earth
articles.rephrased_article: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, a decorated Indian Air Force pilot and test pilot, has published his memoir "The Second Orbit" shortly after returning from the Axiom-4 Mission. The book explores the emotional journey of an astronaut, focusing on doubt, belief, and persistence.  Shukla's writing reflects not only the science and spectacle of spaceflight but also the inner life of an astronaut.  Endorsements for the book highlight its significance, with India's first astronaut, Rakesh Sharma, calling it a "master class" and Sachin Tendulkar praising its inspirational quality. The book underscores the collective aspiration tied to India's space program and is being published by Penguin Books at the end of this month.

articles.title: 2 Men Drown In River While Swimming And Making Reels In UP's Gorakhpur
articles.rephrased_article: Two men, Shivam Kumar (21) and Golu Kumar (19), drowned in the Rapti river near Kartahari village, Gorakhpur, while filming a social media reel with friends. The incident occurred when one of the youths drifted into deeper water and struggled for help, prompting another friend to attempt a rescue. Both men were swept away and their bodies were recovered by rescuers after an extensive search.

articles.title: Accused can't be denied access to documents forming part of charge sheet: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that an accused cannot be denied access to documents forming part of the charge sheet, even if they are considered "highly confidential" for national security reasons.  In a case involving retired Major General V.K. Singh, who is facing prosecution under the Official Secrets Act, the court ordered the CBI to provide a typed copy of the relevant documents with conditions that they not be made public. The Supreme Court emphasized that withholding such documents could prejudice an accused's right to a fair trial and balanced national security concerns.  The order sets aside the High Court's modification of the trial court's order and directs the CBI to provide the documents within two months.

articles.title: Delhi Court Rules Husband Cannot Cite Unemployment To Evade Family Duty
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court ruled that a husband cannot avoid his financial responsibility towards his minor son by claiming unemployment. The court ordered the man to pay Rs 6,000 per month in maintenance for the child until he reaches adulthood.  The appellate court overturned a trial court's decision denying the woman relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence (PWDV) Act, finding that the husband had failed to financially support the child since 2015. The court emphasized that the husband was capable of paying maintenance and directed him to do so.

articles.title: Inside Krushna Abhishek's Luxurious Mumbai Home
articles.rephrased_article: Krushna Abhishek hosted Farah Khan at his Mumbai home, showcasing the comedian's humble beginnings in a 1BHK flat. The tour highlighted the spacious apartment with features like a sleek black kitchen, an earthy living room, and a glamorous glam room. Interior designer Mita Mehta, founder of Mita Mehta Studio, explained how to balance visual appeal for Instagram with practicality and comfort in home design.

articles.title: Imtiaz Ali was once abducted from his college hostel in a cycle rickshaw: ‘Come with us’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Imtiaz Ali, a renowned filmmaker, recalled being abducted from his Delhi University hostel by a local political gang during his college days. The incident stemmed from a disagreement over the placement of a political poster on the wall of his hostel. Ali had asked the group to move the poster to the side walls but they ignored him and pasted it on the front.  The situation escalated when the gang leader confronted Ali, leading to a misunderstanding and ultimately, his escape from the situation.

articles.title: Right to travel abroad of accused must be balanced with victim’s right to speedy trial: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India has overturned a decision by the Telangana High Court that allowed a businessman accused of criminal conspiracy and abetment of suicide to travel to the U.S. for medical treatment. The court ruled that the businessman's right to travel abroad cannot be prioritized over his right to a speedy trial, citing his repeated attempts to circumvent legal proceedings and obtain temporary travel permissions while remaining on a suspended look out circular.  The court emphasized that a balance must be struck between individual liberty and the need for effective criminal justice administration.

articles.title: Chinese Actor Jin Ze dies at 33; agency confirms he passed away at home | Entertainment News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jin Ze, a Chinese actor known for his roles in romance dramas and short-form series, has died at the age of 33. His agency confirmed his passing on June 4th, stating he passed away at home in Hangzhou.  The cause of death has not been disclosed. Shengshi Guangnian Culture Co., Ltd. expressed condolences to his family and urged fans to respect their privacy as they arrange funeral arrangements. The actor's sudden death has shocked fans and sparked widespread tributes online.

articles.title: 'Thought I Would Perish': Everest Survivor Dawa Sherpa Recounts Ordeal
articles.rephrased_article: Dawa Sherpa, a 57-year-old Nepali mountaineer, survived nearly a week on Mount Everest after going missing on May 30. He was found crawling towards base camp by the Sagarmatha Pollution Control Committee (SPCC) on June 4 and is now recovering in Kathmandu from frostbite, dehydration, and a fractured thigh bone.  Dawa Sherpa, known as "Hillary" after legendary climber Edmund Hillary, survived by chewing ice and rationing snacks. The incident has sparked both celebration among fellow climbers and anger from family members who accused rescue teams of failing to locate him sooner.

articles.title: Goa Student Dies By Suicide After Viral Littering Video, Social Media Trolling
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old college student from Goa, Samuel de Braganca, allegedly shot himself dead after a video of him littering went viral on social media. Police registered a case against the student and issued a notice following the video's circulation, which led to public criticism and online trolling.  The student reportedly died by suicide using a firearm belonging to his family, and investigators are examining the circumstances surrounding his death.

articles.title: Higher qualifications cannot always be considered for lower eligibility posts: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India ruled that a person with higher qualifications cannot be selected for a job clearly meant for candidates with lower qualifications. The court overturned the Madras High Court decision which reinstated an employee who had disclosed only passing the 10th standard despite being a graduate, stating that public employment should be made available to all eligible candidates based on prescribed qualifications.  The court acknowledged the employer's need to have the right people at the right place but emphasized that over-qualification cannot be a disqualification and must not be used arbitrarily or discriminatorily.

Police, the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD), and local authorities are investigating the incident.  The victim was taken to shore but pronounced dead despite efforts from paramedics. The DPIRD is urging residents to report any shark sightings.

articles.title: Why Apple’s AI strategy may be the biggest focus at its developer conference next week | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Apple is expected to unveil its new AI strategy at WWDC, focusing on how it plans to integrate AI into its devices and services. The company will showcase an upgraded Siri powered by Google's Gemini AI technology, aiming to deliver a more personalized experience across Apple products.  While Apple has historically focused on privacy-first approaches, the company is facing pressure to leverage AI for everyday user needs and create seamless interactions with AI agents. Whether Apple can successfully integrate AI into its ecosystem and overcome consumer skepticism remains to be seen.

articles.title: Suresh Wadkar met wife Padma when she was 8: ‘Why shouldn’t I marry her?’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Suresh Wadkar, a veteran playback singer, shared his love story with wife Padma Wadkar. articles.title: ‘They said being 30 was old for rom-coms,’ says Taapsee: ‘You dare say that about Shah Rukh’ | Bollywood News - The Indian Express

articles.title: How to Share a Link to a Particular Phrase | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Modern browsers, including Chrome, Safari, and Firefox, offer a feature called "Copy Link to Highlight" that allows users to share specific paragraphs or sentences from web pages. This feature works by creating a URL that includes enough information for the browser to find and highlight the selected text, making it easier to share excerpts in context. The feature is based on a web standard called Text fragments, which has been implemented across browsers for years. While this feature doesn't work with paywalled websites or PDFs, sharing a highlighted link can be more useful than taking screenshots.

articles.title: Velotric Nomad 2 Fat Tire Ebike, Tested and Reviewed (2026) | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: A reviewer tested the Velotric Nomad 2, a new step-through ebike with a comfortable design and powerful motor. articles.rephrased_article: Chipolo, a company known for its Bluetooth trackers, has secured exclusive collaborations with Apple and Google.  The company offers a range of products including the Chipolo Pop, Loop, and Card, as well as bundles compatible with both iOS and Android devices. These trackers use Bluetooth connectivity and GPS to help users locate their belongings. Tile, another popular tracker brand, has a wide variety of forms including stickers, key rings, and wallets. The article highlights the importance of choosing a tracker that fits your needs and lifestyle while considering factors such as battery life, range, and compatibility.

articles.title: Beyond short circuit: Potential fire accidents lurk behind old and overloaded electric wires in Telangana’s building - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana is grappling with a surge in electrical fires attributed to "short circuits", which experts say often mask deeper problems like aging wiring and overloaded systems.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reported 1,042 electrical short circuit incidents in the country in 2024, resulting in 1,012 deaths and 52 injuries. State Fire Department officials emphasize the need for regular rewiring assessments, especially in buildings over 10-15 years old, to ensure safety.  However, concerns persist about the availability of cheaper, substandard electrical materials that often lack proper BIS certification.  The Electricity department acknowledges a regulatory blind spot, with most residential installations relying on self-certification and owner responsibility rather than routine inspections.

articles.title: “They are psychopaths”: Matt Walsh erupts after Jesse Ridgway and Ashley end pregnancy over Down syndrome diagnosis - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jesse Ridgway and his wife Ashley announced they had terminated a pregnancy after doctors diagnosed their unborn child with Down syndrome.  Matt Walsh, a political commentator, criticized the couple's decision, calling them "psychopaths" who would be imprisoned for life. Ridgway acknowledged the experience was traumatic but argued that Down syndrome is objectively difficult for both the child and family. He also expressed support for those living with Down syndrome.

articles.title: How did ChudTheBuilder’s bond payment end JiDion and Alex Rosen’s partnership? Inside the growing controversy - The Times of India

JiDion expressed disapproval of the donation, believing it could have been used for more beneficial purposes and criticized Rosen's past comments and views. articles.title: Consumer rights panel in Kerala orders boutique to pay ₹58,350 for delayed gown delivery as photoshoot called off - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kollam, Kerala

Jennifer Shah, the customer, filed a complaint against Eha Designs Private Limited and its Managing Director, alleging a deficiency in service that led to the cancellation of her scheduled photoshoot. The court ordered the boutique to refund the full price of the gown and pay compensation for emotional distress.

articles.title: “You and your fake husband....": Candace Owens accuses Laura Loomer of lying about her marriage in explosive social media feud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens have escalated their public feud, exchanging personal attacks after Loomer questioned Owens's motives for traveling to Russia. articles.title: Fact check: Did Tyla really get N3on kicked out of a Celebrity Dinner in Monaco? What really happened during the livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: N3on, a streamer, was embroiled in controversy after social media users falsely claimed singer Tyla had him removed from a celebrity dinner in Monaco. The rumor spread quickly online, with clips from a live stream racking up millions of views and fueling speculation about an encounter between the two.  However, viewers soon identified the woman in the video as an Instagram model, not Tyla, highlighting the dangers of viral misinformation.

articles.title: PM Narendra Modi's Yoga Guru HR Nagendra To Lead International Day of Yoga Event At New York's Times Square
articles.rephrased_article: HR Nagendra, yoga guru to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, will lead International Day of Yoga (IDY) celebrations at Times Square in New York on June 21.  He will also inaugurate a special Yoga and wellness retreat in Monticello, New York, from June 12 to 14. The theme for this year's IDY is 'Yoga for Healthy Aging'.

articles.title: HP introduces ZGX Fury GB300, an AI workstation for large-scale models | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: HP unveiled the ZGX Fury GB300 workstation, powered by Nvidia's Grace Blackwell Ultra platform. Designed to bring data center-class AI capabilities to enterprise desktops, the system can support models with up to one trillion parameters and features a large unified memory pool of up to 784GB.  This allows for local processing of AI models and datasets without relying heavily on external storage or cloud infrastructure. The workstation is expected to appeal primarily to large enterprises who require local AI processing for security, compliance, or performance reasons.

articles.title: Dara: Bangaranga singer says she almost quit Eurovision
articles.rephrased_article: Dara, the Bulgarian Eurovision Song Contest winner, revealed she considered quitting due to mental health concerns and anxieties surrounding her ADHD diagnosis.  She initially felt unworthy after being announced as Bulgaria's first entry since 2022. Dara sought professional help from a therapist, which helped her manage stage fright and navigate the intense pressure of Eurovision. Her victory in Vienna was historic, securing Bulgaria its first-ever win in the competition.  Dara now plans to focus on her personal life, including starting a family.

articles.title: Anthony Head: Tributes to Buffy and Ted Lasso star Anthony Head after death aged 72
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Head, the British actor best known for his roles in "Buffy the Vampire Slayer," "Ted Lasso," and "Merlin," died at age 72.  Head's daughters, Emily and Daisy, confirmed his passing from complications due to pneumonia, stating he was surrounded by his family.  Tributes poured in from fellow actors including Sarah Michelle Gellar, David Boreanaz, and Brett Goldstein, who described Head as a kind, talented, and beloved colleague.  Head also enjoyed a successful stage career and appeared in numerous popular British shows throughout his long career.

articles.title: When will Taylor Swift get married? Fans have some ideas
articles.rephrased_article: Rumors and speculation about Taylor Swift's wedding date continue to circulate among her fans, nicknamed Swifties.  The Grammy-winning artist has been coy about the details of her upcoming nuptials with American football star Travis Kelce, but hints have suggested a large guest list and potential numerological significance to the date. Fans are speculating various dates, including June 7th, June 13th, July 6th, and July 4th, based on Swift's past album releases and personal preferences. While some online prediction markets and media outlets have offered guesses about possible guest lists, Swift has yet to confirm any details.  The secrecy surrounding the event is a testament to her desire for privacy while also fueling fan excitement.

articles.title: Man dies in Western Australia after shark attack | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A 35-year-old man died after being bitten by a shark while spearfishing near Albany, Western Australia. Police say the incident occurred off Michaelmas Island, where a witness reported seeing a 4.5-meter shark of an unknown species. The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development urged caution in the area due to increased shark sightings. This is the fourth shark fatality this year in Australia.

articles.title: Bandar box office collection Day 1: Anurag Kashyap’s Bobby Deol film fails to cross Rs 1 cr | Bollywood News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Anurag Kashyap's prison drama "Bandar" opened to a disappointing box office performance, earning Rs 50 lakh net on its first day. The film fell short of crossing the Rs 1 crore mark and had an overall occupancy of 12.58%. Despite performing better than Nishaanchi, which grossed Rs 25 lakh on its opening day despite more shows, "Bandar" trails behind Kashyap's previous films like "Dobaaraa" and "Mukkabaaz". The film also faces stiff competition from recent tentpole releases.

articles.title: Peddi makers to change Janhvi Kapoor scenes after intense backlash: 'Decided to make changes to the concerned portions'
articles.rephrased_article: Jahnvi Kapoor's scenes in the film "Peddi" have been altered after receiving backlash from viewers who found certain aspects of the movie objectifying and inappropriate. Buchi Babu Sana, the director, issued a statement acknowledging the criticism and promising to make changes to the controversial portions of the film.  He stated that he respects women and had not intended to disrespect any female character in the film, but will be making adjustments to ensure it aligns with audience expectations.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out Lockdown Mode to protect against prompt injection attacks | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI has introduced Lockdown Mode, a new security feature for its ChatGPT service. This optional setting restricts several advanced features and capabilities to mitigate prompt injection attacks, which involve manipulating AI models into revealing sensitive information.  Lockdown Mode does not prevent all prompt injections but reduces the likelihood of attackers exploiting network requests or connected tools. The feature is primarily designed for individuals and organizations handling sensitive data and prioritizing security over convenience.

articles.title: Malviya nagar fire, Over 500 Killed In Delhi Fire Accidents In 6 Years, Data Shows, Anaj Mandi fire, Upahar fire tragedy
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi has experienced a significant increase in fire-related deaths and injuries over the past six years. The city's recent tragedy at Flourish Stays B&B highlights ongoing concerns about fire safety measures.

articles.title: Earthquake Of Magnitude 5 Hits Himachal Pradesh
articles.rephrased_article: A 5.0 magnitude earthquake struck near Dharamsala, Himachal Pradesh on Friday night at 10:04 pm, causing tremors felt in Kangra, Chamba, and adjoining districts. The epicenter was located near Dhar Godoi in Kangra district, with a depth of 5 km. The National Center for Seismology reported the earthquake's intensity as moderate.  While no casualties or significant damage have been reported, officials noted that the region falls within Seismic Zone 5, which poses high risk of damage from earthquakes.

articles.title: Malayalam poet A.C. Sreehari passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A.C. Sreehari, a renowned Malayalam poet and academic, passed away on Friday night at the age of 56 due to a heart attack.  He was a former head of the Department of English at Payyanur College and retired in April.  Sreehari's works, including "Yuva Kavithakkoottam" and "Kavithayude Noottandu," are widely studied in Kerala universities. He is survived by his wife Sangeetha K. and son A.C. Sreeharshan. Pinarayi Vijayan, Leader of the Opposition, has expressed condolences on the poet's passing.

articles.title: Mind Games: Mentalist leaves audience spellbound - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu’s Huddle, a conclave of influential experts and thought leaders, concluded its first day in Bengaluru with a performance by mentalist Naman Anand.  Anand's interactive session included illusions, tricks, and the identification of personal details, providing a welcome change from the serious discussions that preceded it. The event featured sessions on topics such as India-China relations, leadership, mental health, and business, with speakers including Dr. Narayan Lakshman, D.K. Shivakumar, and Omar Abdullah.  The conclave is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

articles.title: Between visibility and storytelling: Huma Qureshi and Kritika Kamra on Bollywood’s future - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Huma Qureshi and Kritika Kamra, two Bollywood actors, expressed concerns about a decline in film production in the industry. They also discussed the importance of young aspiring actors participating in filmmaking processes and advocated for pay parity and more diverse roles for women in Bollywood.

articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI has introduced Lockdown Mode, a new security feature for its ChatGPT service. articles.title: 11 Days After Their Deaths, Man Found Dead Clutching Wife, Son's Graves In Uttar Pradesh
articles.rephrased_article: Subhan Ahmad, a 40-year-old man from Madhya Pradesh, was found dead at the graves of his wife and son in Uttar Pradesh's Mahoba district.  His six-year-old son, Hasnain, died from heatwave effects on May 25th, followed by his mother, Rajia Khatoon, who succumbed to shock soon after. Subhan had been deeply grieving for the past eleven days and was found lying motionless near their graves. A relative believes that he may have been bitten by a poisonous insect while at the cemetery, but the exact cause of death is pending a post-mortem report.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out Lockdown Mode to protect against prompt injection attacks | Technology News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI has introduced Lockdown Mode, a new security feature for its ChatGPT service. This optional setting restricts several advanced features to protect against prompt injection attacks, which involve attackers manipulating AI systems to steal data.  Lockdown Mode does not prevent all prompt injections but reduces the likelihood of an attacker exploiting network requests or tools to extract sensitive information. The feature is available to all ChatGPT users and can be enabled through the Safety and Security section of ChatGPT settings.

articles.title: Delhi court flags economic abuse as man pays no child support for 10 years, orders maintenance | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A Delhi court ordered a man to pay Rs 6,000 per month in maintenance to his minor son.  The court found that the husband's claim of unemployment and other financial responsibilities did not absolve him from supporting his child, noting that maintenance is intended to prevent destitution and vagrancy. The judge rejected the husband's argument that the wife was capable of earning and emphasized that actual earnings are distinct from educational qualifications.  The court also found that the trial court erred in dismissing the wife's complaint under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

articles.title: Pune court allows Sugandha Hiremath’s suit in Kalyani family dispute to continue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Pune court has refused to stay a partition suit filed by Sugandha Hiremath, seeking her share in the estimated billions of dollars worth of ancestral wealth belonging to the Kalyani family. The court rejected applications for a stay from Gaurishankar Kalyani and his daughter, Sheetal Kalyani, who argued that Hiremath's suit was similar to others concerning the same family wealth. The court found that while multiple suits exist regarding the Kalyani family's assets, they are distinct in their claims and causes of action.  The court concluded that each suit is independent and does not affect the outcome of others.

articles.title: Can adopted child inherit under Muslim Law? Madras High Court says no | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court ruled that adoption does not create inheritance rights under Muslim personal law, upholding the dismissal of a partition suit seeking property ownership from a deceased woman's late grandmother. The court emphasized that Islamic jurisprudence prohibits adoption and that biological lineage is paramount in succession according to Shariat law.  The court rejected claims of adoption by Gulab John, who was raised as Piyaru Bi’s daughter, finding that she was not the biological daughter but rather the adopted child of Piyaru Bi's sister. The ruling clarified that inheritance rights flow through biological parents and that closer relatives are prioritized in succession.

articles.title: Farah Khan stunned by Terence Lewis' surreal Salvador Dalí bathroom, throne-like commode
articles.rephrased_article: Terence Lewis, a celebrity choreographer and reality show judge, recently gave Farah Khan, a filmmaker-choreographer, a tour of his opulent Mumbai house. The home features luxurious yet elegant decor elements like metallic accents on the entrance door, plush seating in white and beige tones, and a black piano.  Ishitta Arun, an artisan from Jaipur, sourced an antique-style door with detailed carvings for the living space. Farah Khan joked that the bathroom resembled a set from a Sanjay Leela Bhansali film, inspired by the surreal, molten-style basin designed by Terence Lewis in homage to Salvador Dalí.  The tour also included a cozy study and a kitchen with a striking chandelier made of tea kettles.

articles.title: Correcting ‘discrepancies’ is normal practice in statistical exercise, says Census official - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The House Listing Operation in Rajasthan is still underway as part of the multi-pronged Census process, according to an official from the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI). Enumerators are collecting data through house-to-house visits and supervisors are conducting field inspections to ensure accuracy.  However, reports have emerged suggesting that enumerators in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan are being asked to revisit households and correct data discrepancies, particularly on issues like open defecation and access to electricity or cooking gas connections.

articles.title: Two killed, four injured in roof collapse at underground coal mine in Madhya Pradesh’s Shahdol - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) workers were killed and others injured when a portion of the roof collapsed in an underground coal mine in Madhya Pradesh's Shahdol district. The accident occurred at Bangwar mine, where workers were constructing a stopping wall, trapping them under debris. Dhanpuri Police Station House Officer (SHO) Khem Singh Pendro confirmed two workers died and four others were injured. Rescue teams and officials are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Balan The Boy trailer: Mother with a gun will stop at nothing for her son. Watch | Malayalam News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Balan – The Boy, a Malayalam mother-son drama directed by Chidambaram and Jithu Madhavan, premiered its trailer on Friday. articles.title: Neetu Kapoor praises Ranbir-Alia parenting style

articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, a leading AI company, has urged AI labs to pause development of advanced AI systems due to concerns about rapid technological advancement outpacing societal control mechanisms. articles.title: Everest guide survived six-day ordeal by eating chocolate and 'chewing ice'
articles.rephrased_article: Dawa Sherpa, a Nepali guide, survived six days trapped in a crevasse on Mount Everest after his oxygen ran out. He was found by a cleanup team and airlifted to Kathmandu where he is recovering from dehydration, frostbite, and a fractured bone. Chris Thrall, the climber who last saw Sherpa alive, described seeing him "crawling" down the mountain towards Base Camp.  Sherpa survived by chewing ice and eating chocolates he found in his pocket.

articles.rephrased_article: Priya Narayanaswamy, a mother of two, returned to India after her husband's suicide in the wake of job losses and visa complications.
